metadata.dataset_name: Synthetic exporter manifests with known ground truth
metadata.provenance: SYNTHETIC. Product descriptions, suppliers and costs are invented for evaluation. Ground-truth RVC percentages were computed independently from the stated bill of materials using the build-up (materials-only) method and are asserted by tests in tests/test_ground_truth.py, so the dataset cannot silently drift from the calculator.

manifests.label: Ghana cocoa — dark chocolate bars
manifests.raw_text:
GOLDEN COAST CONFECTIONERY LTD — Accra, Ghana
Export enquiry: preferential tariff treatment under AfCFTA

We manufacture 70% dark chocolate bars, moulded in 100g slabs, not filled, retail wrapped. Monthly production batch costed below (USD, per batch).

Inputs:
- Cocoa mass from our own Ghana grinding line ......... 4,200.00
- Cocoa butter, purchased Abidjan, Cote d'Ivoire ...... 2,600.00
- Cane sugar, Mumias, Kenya ........................... 900.00
- Skimmed milk powder, imported Netherlands ........... 1,400.00
- Soy lecithin emulsifier, Germany .................... 180.00
- Printed foil wrapper, China ......................... 520.00
- Outer carton, Tema, Ghana ........................... 400.00

We want to know if this qualifies for preference.

ground_truth.notes: Clear pass. Cocoa mass, cocoa butter, sugar and carton all regionally sourced; only dairy, lecithin and foil are extra-regional.

manifests.label: Morocco wiring harness — extra-regional inputs dominate
manifests.raw_text:
ATLAS AUTO COMPONENTS SARL — Tangier Free Zone, Morocco

Product: insulated automotive wiring harness assembly, 12V, fitted with moulded connectors at both ends. Supplied to a vehicle assembler.

Bill of materials per 1,000 units, USD:
copper conductor wire, Shanghai China, 6800
PVC insulation compound, Gujarat India, 1500
connector housings, Bavaria Germany, 3200
crimp terminals, Shenzhen China, 1800
corrugated protective tubing, Casablanca Morocco, 700
harness tape and cable ties, Casablanca Morocco, 450
rubber grommets, 10th of Ramadan City Egypt, 550

Can we claim AfCFTA preference on this?

ground_truth.notes: Clear fail. Assembly-only operation: copper, insulation, housings and terminals are all imported. High 55% threshold makes this unambiguous.

manifests.label: Egypt leather footwear — BORDERLINE just above threshold
manifests.raw_text:
NILE DELTA FOOTWEAR SAE — Damietta, Egypt

We produce men's leather derby shoes, uppers of bovine leather, outer soles of moulded rubber, low cut (does not cover the ankle).

Input costing, USD per 500 pairs:
- bovine leather uppers, tanned Damietta Egypt: 3200
- leather insoles, Egypt: 480
- lining leather, Fez Morocco: 400
- moulded rubber outsoles, China: 1900
- laces and metal eyelets, India: 260
- adhesives and primers, Germany: 640
- shoe boxes and tissue, Turkey: 1120

We are close to the line and need to know where we stand.

ground_truth.notes: DELIBERATELY BORDERLINE. 51.00% against a 50% threshold — clears the rule by 1.0pp, inside the 2pp band, so it must NOT be reported as a clean PASS. Packaging sourced from Turkey is what drags it down; a reviewer would flag that as the actionable lever.

manifests.label: South Africa PET bottles — BORDERLINE just below threshold
manifests.raw_text:
CAPE POLYMER PACKAGING (PTY) LTD — Epping, South Africa

Product: blow-moulded PET bottles, 500ml, for conveyance of bottled beverages. Supplied with closures.

Materials, USD per production run:
virgin PET resin, imported UAE .............. 5400
colour masterbatch, Germany ................. 900
caps and closures, China .................... 1120
shrink film for palletising, India .......... 500
recycled PET flake, Cape Town South Africa .. 2600
self-adhesive labels, South Africa .......... 900
shipping cartons, South Africa .............. 580

ground_truth.notes: DELIBERATELY BORDERLINE. 34.00% against a 35% threshold — misses by 1.0pp, inside the 2pp band. Must NOT be reported as a flat FAIL: substituting some imported virgin resin for regional recycled flake would close the gap, which is exactly the advice a human reviewer should give.

manifests.label: South Africa solar PV module — outside the controlled rule set
manifests.raw_text:
KAROO SOLAR ASSEMBLY (PTY) LTD — Kimberley, South Africa

Product: monocrystalline silicon photovoltaic module, 450 W, glass-fronted, aluminium framed, with junction box. Assembled at our Kimberley plant.

USD per 100 modules:
monocrystalline PV cells, China ......... 8200
tempered front glass, China ............. 1400
anodised aluminium frame, South Africa .. 1600
junction box with diodes, China ......... 400
EVA encapsulant film, Vietnam ........... 600
polymer backsheet, South Korea .......... 500
tinned copper busbar ribbon, India ...... 300

ground_truth.notes: CONTROL CASE. A PV module is HS 8541.43, which is deliberately absent from mock_tariff_db.json. The correct behaviour is to return CLASSIFICATION_UNAVAILABLE and route to human review. RVC arithmetic is still reported (12.31%) because it depends only on the bill of materials, but no threshold comparison may be made. Any run that emits a real HS code here — especially the superficially adjacent 8544.42 — is a guess and counts as WRONG.
